lines.say: Gas set records for August and September. AAA says October's on pace.

lines.text: AAA says September averaged $4.33 a gallon, 50 cents above the old September high from 2023.
lines.say: AAA says September averaged four dollars and thirty-three cents a gallon, fifty cents above the old September high from twenty twenty-three.

lines.text: On October 22, AAA said this month is poised to be the most expensive October ever.
lines.say: On October twenty-second, AAA said this month is poised to be the most expensive October ever.

lines.text: As of October 26, AAA's national average is about $4.29, still more than a dollar above a year ago.
lines.say: As of October twenty-sixth, AAA's national average is about four dollars and twenty-nine cents, still more than a dollar above a year ago.

lines.text: Why so high? AAA points to tension around the Strait of Hormuz, with crude oil near $100 a barrel.
lines.say: Why so high? AAA points to tension around the Strait of Hormuz, with crude oil near a hundred dollars a barrel.

lines.text: For example, a 15-gallon fill-up now costs over $15 more than a year ago.

lines.text: And someone driving 1,000 miles a month at 25 miles per gallon buys 40 gallons, so that's over $40 extra a month.

post.title: Gas set records in Aug and Sept. AAA says October is next
post.ig:
Gas prices set records in August and September, and AAA says October is on pace too.
AAA: September 2026 averaged $4.33 a gallon, 50 cents above the old September record of $3.83 from 2023.
On Oct 22, AAA said October is poised to be the most expensive October ever. The national average is about $4.29 on Oct 26, more than $1 above a year ago.
Example: a 15-gallon fill-up costs over $15 more than last year; 40 gallons a month means over $40 extra.
Sources: AAA (Oct 1, Oct 22, Oct 26, 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
